FOLLOW-UP on the rotation-black note: root cause found and fixed from my side, and it touches main.ts (under the maintainer's standing grant). fitCanvas was doing a FULL scale.resize per rotation STAGE (a real phone restages the viewport several times) — traced at ~2s of main-thread stall PER resize in the harness, which is exactly why the OS composited stale letterboxed frames for seconds. main.ts fitCanvas now (a) holds fire while :root.ml-flip is up (hud.ts's rotation transition), (b) ALSO skips when in-game + touch + viewport aspect disagrees with ml-land — the #game ResizeObserver delivers BEFORE the resize event that starts the flip, so the class alone missed the first stage — and (c) listens for the flip's single 'ml-flip-flush' event to apply the final size in ONE resize, hidden under a theme-surface veil (.ml-flip-veil). Desktop and all non-rotation resizes are byte-identical (the guard needs ml-ingame + touch + aspect mismatch). Gate: verify-landscape 4c asserts zero canvas resizes before the flush and the single re-fit after. smoke/mobile/gamepad/dropqty/chatpage/bars all green. If you'd rather own a different shape for the canvas-side deferral, shout — the hooks are one class + one event.

That module is the seam: the wiki drawer (wikipanel.ts) asks for a freeze, gamefreeze calls TimeStep.sleep()/wake(). CLAUDE.md gained one entry under the Mobile/PWA section. THE ONE THING WORTH KNOWING IF YOU EVER TOUCH THIS: waking is deliberately NOT TimeStep.resume() — resume() arms Phaser's backgrounded-tab recovery (_coolDown = panicMax = 120), which clamps every delta to the 16.7ms target for the next 120 FRAMES. Measured: 16.7ms of game time per 167ms of real time, and a thawed player walked 20wu where an unfrozen one walked 151 — visible slow motion on anything under 60fps. gamefreeze moves lastTime to now instead, so the first frame back is ~0ms with no cooldown. Separately: Phaser arms that same cooldown from its own window-FOCUS handler, so tapping into the wiki iframe and back out already does it with or without the freeze (verified identical on the unfrozen baseline, _coolDown 116 both ways) — pre-existing, not a freeze bug. Input stops while frozen, which is correct against your WorldRoom: it integrates only what it receives, so a frozen client stands still instead of coasting. npm test 205/205, typecheck clean, verify-smoke and verify-wikibtn green.
